title: Oklahoma State University — Watershed Hydrology & Rangeland Ecology (2 MS positions)
org: Stillwater, OK · Environmental Science Graduate Program
body: Two fully funded MS assistantships — Neosho River Watershed, Oklahoma. Tar Creek Superfund Site contamination context. Position 1: Ecology/Rangeland — wildlife habitat, species of conservation need. Position 2: Hydrology/GIS — site suitability modeling, flood mitigation. Full stipend + tuition waiver + health insurance. Advisors: Dr. Scott Stoodley & Dr. Jaime Schussler. Email: esgp@okstate.edu
desc: Two fully funded MS assistantships for an interdisciplinary watershed conservation project in the Neosho River Watershed of northeastern Oklahoma — which includes the Tar Creek Superfund Site, one of the most historically significant mining-contaminated landscapes in the US. Position 1 (Ecology/Rangeland): wildlife habitat assessment, species of conservation need, restoration planning. Position 2 (Hydrology/GIS): watershed hydrology, site suitability modeling, flood mitigation, conservation planning. The contaminated watershed + GIS + field ecology combination is a direct methodological parallel to Erin’s Pigeon River lead contamination capstone. Advisors: Dr. Scott Stoodley & Dr. Jaime Schussler.

more: Project details This is an NSF-FIRE funded project investigating how "whiplashes" (back-to-back extreme wet/dry events) in moisture patterns drive forest hydrology and flammability across southeastern landscapes. The student will work with an interdisciplinary team at MSU, NC State, and the USDA Forest Service. Work includes quantifying regional fuel loadings and conducting field-scale fuel moisture dynamic experiments. detail.v: About the program

The USGS Recent Graduate Program is a formal federal hiring pathway. Participants complete a structured 1–2 year developmental experience, receive mentoring, and can be non-competitively converted to permanent federal positions at the end. This is a meaningful career accelerator for someone targeting a federal water resources or environmental science career.
How to find the right position

Search USAJobs for "USGS Recent Graduate" and filter by series: 1315 (Hydrology), 1350 (Geology), 0401 (Biology), 0408 (Ecology). Also search 1301 (Physical Science). Prioritize Water Science Center positions — SAWSC (NC/SC/GA), Southeast (FL/AL/MS), and Appalachians WSC are the strongest regional fits.

title: Physical Scientist (Environmental) — Air Force PALACE Acquire recent-graduate program
org: U.S. Air Force — Air Force Civilian Career Training
body: This is the environmental physical-scientist track of the Air Force PALACE Acquire program, the sibling posting to the biological-scientist track already on your list. PALACE Acquire is the Air Force's centrally funded recent-graduate development program: you enter at GS-07 or GS-09, follow a three-year formal training plan with built-in yearly salary increases, and convert to a permanent civilian position on completion. The work centers on environmental monitoring, contamination assessment, and environmental compliance support at Air Force installations, across 48 named sites including Gunter and Maxwell AFB in Alabama, Davis-Monthan in Arizona, Edwards, Los Angeles, Travis and Vandenberg in California, and the Air Force Academy and Buckley in Colorado. This is a genuine nationwide permanent-hire pipeline, not one of the resume-bank placeholder announcements that dominate federal natural-resources searches.
desc: One thing to check before you spend time on this: the physical-scientist track has a different basic requirement than the biological one. It asks for a degree in physical science, engineering, or mathematics that includes at least 24 semester hours of physical science or related engineering science. An Environmental Science BS often clears that through chemistry, geology, hydrology and soils coursework, but it depends on your specific transcript — count those hours before applying. If you do qualify, this is arguably the better-matched of the two PALACE tracks for you: contamination assessment and environmental monitoring is precisely what your Pigeon River lead and trace-metal sediment capstone was. Your 3.731 GPA also clears the Superior Academic Achievement threshold of 2.95, which is what qualifies you for direct GS-07 entry rather than GS-05.

detail.v: The one-year requirement — what it actually means

Verified against the live posting on Aug 18, 2026. This vacancy is classified Natural Resources Planner II, grade 15. The minimum qualification is an environmental science or natural resources bachelor’s PLUS one year of experience in natural resources planning or applied environmental science. The degree half you meet outright; the experience half you do not clearly meet.

detail.label: What could count
detail.value: AmeriCorps NCCC, Feb–Nov 2019 — about ten months. It is the only entry in your history in the right category. Your resume currently describes it as recruitment events and nonprofit sponsorship coordination; if the term involved conservation fieldwork, describe that instead — the current wording undersells it badly.

detail.label: Maryland counts volunteer work
detail.value: The state application form says verbatim: "List below, beginning with your most recent position, all of your work experience including military service and all volunteer activities." AmeriCorps belongs in that section, not just on a resume.

detail.label: Do not rely on a resume
detail.value: The same form says "do not submit a resume in lieu of completing this portion of the application." Fill the work-experience section in fully or you can be screened out on process alone.

detail.v: Two ways around it

detail.label: Planner I needs no experience
detail.value: The same classification series has a Natural Resources Planner I with the identical bachelor’s requirement and zero years of experience. You are qualified for that level today — watch MDE and DNR for Planner I openings.

detail.label: A master’s waives the year
detail.value: A master’s in natural resources planning, management, development, environmental/urban/regional planning, resource economics, environmental system management, water or land resources planning, environmental landscape architecture, or the physical, biological, chemical or environmental sciences substitutes for the required experience outright. This is a concrete reason to keep the grad track moving.

detail.label: The list outlives the vacancy
detail.value: Successful candidates are ranked Best Qualified and placed on the eligible (employment) list for at least one year, so a strong application keeps working after this particular post is filled.

title: Working in Canada as a US citizen — the two permit routes (READ FIRST)
org: Immigration reference · applies to every Canadian entry below
pills: IEC = open permit, no job offer
metaLine: 🇨🇦 The jobs are real and the work matches — the question is which permit gets you there
body: Canadian conservation work maps almost one-to-one onto Erin’s training, but a US citizen needs authorisation. Two routes are open to her. (1) INTERNATIONAL EXPERIENCE CANADA — Working Holiday. There is no bilateral US–Canada youth-mobility agreement, so Americans cannot apply directly; they go through a Recognized Organization (SWAP, administered in the US by IENA/InterExchange). Ages 18–35. It is an OPEN work permit for up to a year with NO job offer required. (2) CUSMA PROFESSIONAL work permit — LMIA-exempt, which makes employers far more willing, but it requires a job offer in a listed profession.
desc: Read this before working the Canadian list. The IEC route is the one to act on first: an open permit means she can take seasonal field crews and technician work that is effectively unreachable from abroad, and a year of that is exactly the "one year of experience in applied environmental science" that US state wetland and natural-resources roles keep asking for. The CUSMA route matters once she has an offer: the official Appendix 2 list includes Biologist, Forester, Range Manager/Range Conservationalist, Soil Scientist, Entomologist, Zoologist, Horticulturist, Geologist, Land Surveyor, Landscape Architect and Research Assistant — each needing only a "Baccalaureate or Licenciatura Degree" with NO experience minimum. Two cautions: an officer must accept that an Environmental Science BS fits the profession claimed, and government postings are largely a dead end — non-citizens may apply to the Canadian federal public service but citizens and PRs get preference and non-citizens were only about 2.5% of hires.

detail.v: Route 1 — IEC Working Holiday (start here)

detail.label: Why it is best
detail.value: OPEN work permit, up to 12 months, NO job offer needed — she can take any job, including the seasonal field work that builds the experience US employers want.

detail.label: How Americans get in
detail.value: Not directly. The US has no youth-mobility agreement with Canada, so she must be nominated by a Recognized Organization — SWAP (swap.ca), administered stateside by IENA/InterExchange. Places are limited and waitlisted; apply early in the season.

detail.label: Age limit
detail.value: 18–35. She is 28, so there is several years of runway — but this is the one route with an expiry date on it.

detail.v: Route 2 — CUSMA professional (once she has an offer)

detail.label: The advantage
detail.value: LMIA-exempt: the employer does not have to prove no Canadian could do the job, which is the usual deal-breaker. Requires a job offer in a listed profession.

detail.label: Professions that fit her
detail.value: Biologist · Forester · Range Manager/Range Conservationalist · Soil Scientist · Entomologist · Zoologist · Horticulturist · Geologist · Land Surveyor · Landscape Architect · Research Assistant at a post-secondary institution. All require only "Baccalaureate or Licenciatura Degree" — no years of experience.

detail.label: The catch
detail.value: The officer must accept that her degree qualifies her for the profession claimed. Environmental Science read as "Biologist" is plausible given her ecology, wildlife, mammalogy and wetlands coursework, but it is not automatic. A technician-titled role likely will not qualify as Biologist — the separate Scientific Technician/Technologist category covers that and is keyed to theoretical knowledge rather than a specific degree.

detail.v: Route 3 — the long game

detail.label: Canadian funded MSc
detail.value: A Canadian master’s earns a Post-Graduation Work Permit on completion — open, no employer needed — and Canadian work experience is the main input to permanent residence. The grad route and the job route are the same route, just ordered differently.

detail.label: Where NOT to spend effort
detail.value: Federal and provincial government postings, and Parks Canada. Technically open to non-citizens, but citizens and PRs get preference and non-citizens were ~2.5% of hires. Aim at private consultancies and non-profits instead.

title: Funded MSc in Canada — how the money actually works (READ FIRST)
org: Reference · applies to every Canadian graduate entry
stipend: Context: international grad tuition averages ~C$24,000/yr
metaLine: 🇨🇦 A C$26,000 stipend can be worth almost nothing after international tuition — always ask
body: In the United States a funded assistantship normally means a stipend PLUS a tuition waiver, so the stipend is yours to live on. Canada often works differently. Funding packages are frequently designed to OFFSET tuition rather than come on top of it, and international students are charged a higher rate than Canadians — averaging around C$24,000 a year across Canadian graduate programmes. Trent University, for example, states plainly that its graduate funding is "not intended to cover living costs and all fees" and that "funding offsets tuition". Some universities charge international PhD students the domestic rate but still charge international rates for a master’s.
desc: This is the single question that decides whether a Canadian offer is real. A posting advertising "C$25,000–28,000 per year" sounds comparable to a US assistantship, but if international tuition of roughly C$24,000 comes out of it, what is left is not a living. Ask every Canadian supervisor these four things before you invest in an application: (1) Am I charged domestic or international tuition? (2) Does the funding package cover tuition and fees, or is tuition deducted from it? (3) Is there an international tuition scholarship, differential fee waiver, or offset I would be eligible for? (4) What is the actual take-home figure after all fees? None of this makes Canada a bad idea — the degree still earns a three-year open work permit afterwards, which no American programme does. It just means the sticker number needs translating before you compare it to a US offer.

detail.v: The four questions to ask every Canadian supervisor

detail.label: 1. Which tuition rate
detail.value: Am I assessed domestic or international tuition as an American? Some schools charge international rates for a master’s even where PhD students pay domestic.

detail.label: 2. Covered or deducted
detail.value: Does the funding package pay tuition and fees separately, or is tuition taken out of the stipend? This is the difference between a liveable offer and a non-offer.

detail.label: 3. Any offset
detail.value: Is there an international tuition scholarship, differential fee waiver or entrance award I would be eligible for, and is it automatic or a separate application?

detail.label: 4. The real number
detail.value: What does a student in this position actually take home per month after tuition and all ancillary fees? Ask for the net figure, not the headline.

detail.v: What Canada gives you that the US does not

detail.label: A work permit
detail.value: A Canadian master’s earns a Post-Graduation Work Permit of three years — open, no employer needed — and Canadian work experience is the main route to permanent residence. Weigh that against a lower net stipend.

detail.label: Advisor-first culture
detail.value: Canadian MSc positions are usually filled by a professor choosing a student, not by a central admissions committee. Emailing the supervisor is not optional here — it IS the application process.

detail.label: Watch for stale posts
detail.value: Department opportunity pages are rarely pruned. Several Trent listings still show 2025 start dates. Always confirm the position is open before writing anything long.

body: Description : The Davis Herpetology Lab at The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) is seeking a highly motivated M.S. student for a fully funded graduate assistantship (stipend plus tuition covered) beginning in Fall 2027. The successful applicant will develop a thesis project focused on the ecology and conservation of amphibians and reptiles in south Texas. This collaborative project may address topics that include species ecology, conservation biology, distribution, natural history, disease ecology, community ecology, and/or habitat use and are encouraged to incorporate field, laboratory, and museum-based approaches. South Texas contains numerous conservation-priority species whose ecology remains poorly understood, including species such as the Speckled Racer and Mexican Burrowing Toad, providing exceptional opportunities for impactful research. Because the lab emphasizes museum-based biodiversity research, students should be comfortable participating in the ethical scientific collection, euthanasia, and preservation of scientific specimens. Students will receive training in study design, field and laboratory techniques, and data analysis, and are expected to present at scientific conferences and publish their research in peer-reviewed journals. The successful applicant will begin their graduate program in August 2027, with the possibility of being hire
desc: A fully funded MS assistantship where you would develop your own thesis project on amphibian and reptile ecology and conservation in south Texas — the lab explicitly invites topics spanning species ecology, conservation biology, distribution, disease ecology, community ecology and habitat use, with field, laboratory and museum approaches all welcome. It sits in the Science Division rather than a field office, so the work supports research design rather than only data collection — and the posting says organising field programmes, which is planning and coordination responsibility rather than pure execution. And the four-year requirement is met outright by your degree under the year-for-year substitution rule, so you qualify on paper for a permanent state scientific technician position, which is rare at your stage. Freshwater survival of native fish is watershed science by another name: the controlling factors are flow, temperature, sediment and habitat, which is your subject matter with fish as the response variable. Apply to this and the Newaukum posts together — same agency, same deadline, one set of materials.

Four of the listed duties map directly onto things you can already evidence — mapping and site assessments (your multi-criteria GIS suitability work), collecting monitoring data, riparian and stream restoration, and writing it all up. Low-tech process-based stream restoration is a fast-growing specialism and good to have early. It is a term post to May 2028 rather than permanent and depends on continued grant funding, which is normal for joint-venture roles, but nearly two years is real experience and the salary is well above the entry-level conservation band. body: White Oak Conservation runs conservation breeding and recovery programmes for over 30 imperilled species across 600 acres on the St. Mary’s River, surrounded by 22,000 acres of mixed forest and wetlands. The specialist post focuses on avian and canid recovery, with possible work on other taxa such as amphibians. Duties include daily animal care (diet preparation, feeding, cleaning, medicating, observing and training); animal restraint, incubation and hatching, transfers, introductions, operant conditioning, assisted reproduction in cranes and passerine mist-netting; assisting with area research projects; maintaining the surrounding areas for ecological health; assisting veterinary staff with procedures and sample collection; keeping Florida grasshopper sparrow breeding records; organising, preparing and conducting controlled burns and writing the burn plans and after-action reports; and maintaining wildlife records.
desc: Genuinely rare experience — the Florida grasshopper sparrow is one of the most endangered birds in North America, and hands-on recovery work carries real weight on a CV. Parts of the job fit you well: mist-netting, research support, records, and especially the prescribed-burn work, since writing burn plans is a qualification in itself. Be clear-eyed about the rest, though: the core of the day is animal husbandry — feeding, cleaning, medicating, restraint, assisted reproduction — which is closer to zookeeping than to the field ecology you have trained for. Worth applying if captive recovery work appeals; if what you want is landscape-scale field science, the Rio Grande post is the better use of the same effort.

body: The Institute for Wildlife Studies is hiring a full-time Wildlife Biologist on San Clemente Island, starting late September or early October 2026. The project protects federally listed species on the island and develops and tests new methods to manage invasive species. Primary duties include lethal control of non-native predators (feral cats and black rats) and non-lethal management of native island foxes; night-time predator hunting by vehicle and on foot; trapping for predator removal; rat management including trapping and poisoning; trapping, handling, vaccinating and providing veterinary care for island foxes; and data entry and analysis in Word, Excel and Access. desc: Channel Island conservation work is some of the most consequential species-recovery work in the country, and the island fox handling is excellent experience. body: The Palmquist Lab at Marshall University is recruiting a funded MS student to study vegetation dynamics and plant-community change in coastal ecosystems on Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, a sea island in South Carolina. The project builds on a network of 57 permanent vegetation plots installed and sampled in 2022: the student will re-sample them in summer 2027 to measure plant-community change, analyse the largely unexplored 2022 dataset, and can use and potentially improve existing island vegetation maps built from remotely sensed products and field validation points. Coastal plant communities there are structured by salinity, elevation, soil texture, soil moisture, exposure and light. Required: coursework in plant ecology, knowledge of south-eastern US vegetation, strong communication and quantitative skills, and interest in plant-community analysis. The student will serve as a teaching assistant. Funding is a teaching assistantship for two years with supplemental research pay — $24,000 over 12 months — plus a full tuition waiver; the student covers university fees and health insurance. Preferred start January 2027, no later than May 2027. Apply by emailing Dr. Kyle Palmquist a one-page statement, CV, unofficial transcripts and three references, with 'MS position – coastal vegetation' in the subject, no later than October 16, 2026.
desc: Coastal wetland and marsh-edge vegetation, permanent plots, and remote-sensing vegetation maps — squarely inside Erin's wetland and GIS strengths, with a January start that could get her into grad school within four months. body: The Palmquist Lab at Marshall University is recruiting an MS student for a five-year NSF-funded project on how climate change, wildfire and livestock grazing intensity interact to affect big-sagebrush plant communities across their range in the western US. The project uses an individual-based plant simulation model to project community change under future conditions; possible student-led projects include the role of competition in plant functional-type responses and shrub–grass coexistence, or using livestock grazing to curb invasive species and wildfire risk under a future climate. The work includes collaboration with ecologists at Yale University and scientists and managers from BLM, USGS, USFWS, USFS and USDA ARS. Required: coursework in ecology and statistics, knowledge of and experience in western sagebrush ecosystems, strong communication and quantitative skills, and an interest in learning modelling (modelling and programming experience highly desirable). Funding is one year of teaching assistantship and one year of research assistantship — a $24,000 12-month stipend — plus a full tuition waiver; the student covers fees and health insurance. Apply by email to Dr. Kyle Palmquist with a one-page statement, CV, unofficial transcripts and three references ('MS position - dryland plant communities' in the subject) no later than November 2, 2026.

body: NC State is recruiting an MS student to analyse wild turkey gobbling activity and habitat use across the northern Blue Mountains of Oregon and Washington, where the Forest Service is restoring forest structure with silviculture and prescribed fire. body: The Kraskura lab at Towson University is leading a Chesapeake Bay Trust-funded study of how stream restoration affects fish performance, habitat suitability and distribution. Field sampling of fish and stream conditions at sites with different levels of restoration, and lab tests of aerobic scope and swimming capacity, will be collected before the student starts; the MS student will turn those data into a mechanistic habitat suitability model and deliver the results as maps and an interactive tool (for example an R Shiny app) for partners. The assistantship is fully funded for two years with full tuition remission and a stipend averaging $21,500 a year. The student can enrol in either the Biological Sciences or the Environmental Science and Studies thesis track. The deadline is October 15, 2026.
desc: Habitat suitability modelling delivered as maps is a close match to the GIS multi-criteria suitability work Erin has already done, applied to stream restoration. Towson is about two and a half hours from Richmond.

body: This is the companion MS on the same Chesapeake Bay Trust stream-restoration project in the Kraskura lab. The thesis will monitor physiological bioindicators — lipid content, oxidative-stress markers and body condition — in common stream fish across the restoration timeline and across sites with different restoration levels, and will measure how temperature and conductivity affect swimming and aerobic capacity. Those data feed the project's habitat suitability modelling and help judge whether restoration is working. It is fully funded as a research assistantship with full tuition remission and a stipend averaging $21,500 a year for two years. The deadline is October 1, 2026, for a spring 2027 start.
desc: A field-heavy stream restoration MS in the Chesapeake watershed that uses water-quality measurements such as conductivity, close to her capstone work. It closes on October 1, two weeks before the modelling sister position.
